headline: Integrated WGCNA and machine learning nominate candidate hub genes across diseases
label: Machine Learning Hub Gene Discovery
summary: Co-expression networks paired with machine learning feature selection are a common route to candidate diagnostic genes in diverse diseases.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these nine publications is a bioinformatics pipeline that combines weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) or differential expression with machine learning feature selection on public transcriptomic data to nominate candidate hub genes or diagnostic signatures. Examples include six atopic dermatitis hub genes validated in an independent cohort, CARTPT, TOB1, and GLO1 for benign prostatic hyperplasia, and C5AR1, KDM2A, and HCAR3 in inflammatory bowel disease supported by molecular docking. Other items extend the template to oral squamous cell carcinoma prognosis, endometriosis molecular subtyping, ulcerative colitis genes tied to ferroptosis and cuproptosis with single-cell analysis, and platelet-related genes in ulcerative colitis. What is new lies mainly in disease context and added layers such as immune infiltration and single-cell data, while the core method is established. Validation depth varies, from cross-platform and independent-cohort checks to docking and, in one case, experimental validation.
